1  JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 28.02.2020 PASSED IN  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC:32493  MFA No. 1853 of 2022 MVC NO.519/2017 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,
MACT, HASSAN, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE DR. JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri.G.M.Sharath Kumar, learned counsel who argued on behalf of Sri.Chethan.B, learned counsel on record for the appellant.
Also heard Sri.Ashok.N.Patil, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company.

2. Seeking enhancement of compensation this appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Belur in MVC No.519/2017 dated 28.02.2020.
3.

When this Court directed the learned counsel for the appellant to file translated copy of the impugned order, Sri.G.M.Sharath Kumar and Sri.Ashok.N.Patil submits that they will assist the Court in arriving at a just conclusion and therefore, the matter can be disposed of.
In light of the submission thus made, the Court proceeds with the disposal of the matter on merits.
4. The only point urged and raised by the learned counsel for the appellant is that the Tribunal erred in taking the notional income of the appellant.
Learned counsel states that the appellant as a businessman and agriculturist was earning huge sum by the date of accident.
But the Tribunal took the notional income of the appellant as Rs.8,000/- p.m. which is unjustifiable.
5. On the other hand, the submission made by Sri.Ashok.N.Patil is that the appellant failed to produce any substantive proof with regard to the actual occupation and earnings by the date of accident.

However, both the learned counsel did not dispute the fact that the figure adapted by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority as notional income for the relevant period i.e., Rs.9,500/-
can be taken in to consideration for assessing the compensation which is required to be awarded towards NC: 2024:KHC:32493 loss of future earnings on account of permanent physical disability.

sentences.text: After elaborately arguing the case, both the learned counsel requested the Court to award justifiable sum as global compensation.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.30,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.93,000/- towards future medical and incidental expenses, Rs.16,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period, Rs.92,160/- towards loss of future earnings on account of disability and Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.

However, having considered the fact that the Tribunal erred in assessing the notional income of the appellant and as the amount awarded towards compensation for loss of income during laid up period are low, this Court is of the view that a global sum of Rs.30,000/- is required to be enhanced.
The enhancement will make the compensation awarded just and reasonable.

Therefore, the appeal is disposed of with the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:32493 ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The compensation that is awarded by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Belur through orders in MVC No.519/2017 dated 28.02.2020 is enhanced by Rs.30,000/-.
(iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(iv) Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of 8(eight) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.
(v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
